stimuli.description: 5 different sets of unfamiliar cuboid objects (1.5*2.7*4.7 cm) made from LEGOTM bricks, with individual numbers and positions of rectangular structures on the sides. Objects had smooth sides, plain bottom, and nubby upper side. 17 objects were hidden in a small fabric sac for haptic exploration.
Apparatus-based two-point discrimination paradigm using pairs of brass needles (0.7 mm diameter, 200 µm blunt endings) with varying separations (1.0-7.0 mm) applied to fingertips.
Paper-and-pencil version of the non-verbal Raven Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM) test, consisting of 5 sets of tasks with increasing complexity, requiring completion of patterns/structures.

limitations: Gender differences in haptic identification of unfamiliar objects might be influenced by the use of arbitrary instead of familiar objects.
Further studies are needed using familiar objects, although this poses problems because most familiar objects are heavily overlearned.
The absence of correlation between tactile acuity and haptic performance might be attributable in part to the objects used, which were larger than the objects used in some other studies.
